scenario.name: LottieFiles Incident Report, Snyk & Wiz — @lottiefiles/lottie-player NPM Supply Chain Compromise, Unpinned CDN Propagation & Web3 Drainer Injection
scenario.overview: Picture a clean city hospital ward with a red-cross triage check-in desk, curtained patient exam bays, a wall of labeled medicine cabinets, and rolling stainless-steel medical carts. Walking briskly past the hospital triage desk in a borrowed white lab coat, an intruder grabs a spare clipboard and wheels a rolling medical cart down the ward corridor. In this real-world scenario, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the triage nurse's station, then smuggles copied records out past the hospital triage check-in desk in tiny disguised batches. The head triage nurse checks the electronic shift roster at the nurse station and spots a lab-coat visitor who was never assigned to that hospital ward. In this scenario (T1195.002, LottieFiles Incident Report, Snyk & Wiz - @lottiefiles/lottie-player NPM Supply Chain Compromise, Unpinned CDN Propagation & Web3 Drainer Injection), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: compromised NPM Token Pushes, then obfuscated Bundle Execution, then dynamic DOM Overlay Injection. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Compromised NPM Token Pushes, then Obfuscated Bundle Execution, then Dynamic DOM Overlay Injection, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on CloudTrail Event 200 correlated across the documented kill chain.

stages.description: Walking briskly past the hospital triage desk in a borrowed white lab coat, an intruder grabs a spare clipboard and wheels a rolling medical cart down the ward corridor. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder quietly copies a trusted access pass from the triage nurse's station while everyday visitors and the triage nurse go about their routine. Using a compromised maintainer NPM token, the attacker publishes three rapid-fire versions (2.0.5, 2.0.6, and 2.0.7) of @lottiefiles/lottie-player to NPM. Here in Step 2 inside the hospital ward, the intruder leaves a hidden spare latch behind so they can walk back into the hospital ward later without disturbing the sealed clean-supply closet. stages.title: Stage 3: Dynamic DOM Overlay Injection & AceDrainer `eth_sendTransaction` / `Permit2` Signing
stages.subtitle: Impact & Collection (T1185 - Browser Session Hijacking / T1565)
stages.description: Quietly photocopying records onto a hidden notepad while standing beside the exam bay, the intruder wheels the cart right back toward the elevator lobby. In this final step inside the hospital ward, the intruder smuggles copied records out past the hospital triage check-in desk in tiny disguised batches until the nurse station chart audit catches the mismatch. Instructed by wss://castleservices.org, the injected script renders a pixel-perfect modal overlay inside the trusted web app’s DOM prompting the user to "Verify Wallet Connection", tricking them into signing an ERC-20 Permit2 approval or eth_sendTransaction call to the AceDrainer smart contract (logged in SIEM Event 1001 with DrainerFamily=AceDrainer, RpcMethodAbused=eth_signTypedData_v4 / eth_sendTransaction, DefenseControl=Subresource Integrity , SRI + CSP connect-src so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact). Under the hood, the observed step executes document.body.appendChild(walletConnectOverlayModal) -> window.ethereum.request({ method: "eth_signTypedData_v4", params: [victimAddr, permit2Payload] }) (which executes the technical command / telemetry directive , document.body.appendChild, walletConnectOverlayModal -> window.ethereum.request, { method: " so that advances the scenario kill-chain under MITRE T1185 during "Dynamic DOM Overlay Injection & AceDrainer eth_sendTransaction / Permit2 Signing" , Instructed by wss://castleservices while generating verifiable host or network telemetry for DFIR attribution). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ lottie-player.js / ⇠#3 ACK 1001) from Node ③ (#3 NPM & Unpinned CDN (unpkg / jsDelivr @latest)) to Node ④ (#4 Production Web App (@lottiefiles/lottie-player@2.0.7)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 End-User Browser DOM & Web3 Wallet (AceDrainer)).
